questions.prompt: Which forgot-password response best avoids user enumeration?
options: 'If an account exists, we have sent a reset link'
questions.explanation: The same response for existing and unknown emails reveals nothing.

questions.prompt: A password reset link should work only once.
questions.explanation: Reset tokens must be single use, time limited and invalidated after use.

questions.prompt: A user registers as Asha@Example.test and another registration succeeds for asha@example.test. What is the most likely root cause?
options: Email is not normalised and the uniqueness check is case-sensitive
questions.explanation: Emails should be normalised and uniquely constrained to avoid duplicates.

questions.prompt: Which are defects in a password reset implementation? Select all that apply.
options: The token can be used twice
An older token still works after a newer one is requested
questions.explanation: Tokens need single use, expiry and invalidation by newer tokens. A short expiry is correct.

questions.prompt: If a password field silently truncates input longer than 64 characters, a user can end up with a password different from the one they typed.
questions.explanation: Silent truncation breaks later logins and weakens security; reject or accept the full value.

questions.prompt: Password rules: 8 to 64 characters. Which tests probe the boundaries while keeping other rules valid?
questions.explanation: Boundaries are just outside and inside, keeping the content valid so only length is varied.

questions.prompt: The reset link in an email uses the Host header of the request and points to evil.test when the header is modified in an authorised test. What is this?
options: Host header poisoning: build links from configuration, not from request headers
questions.explanation: An attacker could make victims click a link to their site. Use a configured base URL.

questions.prompt: A user changes their password. Which should also happen?
options: Outstanding reset tokens are invalidated and other sessions are ended or reviewed per policy, and the user is notified
questions.explanation: Password change must invalidate old credentials and tokens, and notify the user.

questions.prompt: Email verification link is clicked after 3 days and the account is activated even though the policy says 24 hours. What type of test missed it?
options: State/time-based test for token expiry, such as testing before, at and after the expiry boundary
questions.explanation: Expiry rules are states with time guards; test them with boundary times.
